newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still up late on technical buying.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still up late on technical buying.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained higher late Friday in moderate activity, with stable physical prices and some pre-weekend technical buying and shortcovering still lifting the complex, sources said.
By 1420 EDT, July rallied seven cents to $2.15 per million British thermal units, while August was 5.4 cents higher at $2.16. Other deferreds were steady to up 4.7 cents.
"We started off with shortcovering, then locals went for the (buy) stops on the way up," said a New York futures trader, noting July's higher close yesterday signaled a possible technical reversal.
While some chart traders remained skeptical about further gains, they agreed a higher close again today could mean more buying next week, particularly if the South heats up as forecast.
July support was still pegged at $2.055, with psychological buying expected at $2. Resistance was now seen at $2.21, $2.25 and then at the recent highs in the $2.37 area.
Despite a more supportive weather forecast next week, traders noted temperatures in the Midwest and Northeast were expected to hover around normal, a factor likely to temper the bulls.

In the cash Friday, gas at the Louisiana Gulf was talked little changed in the low-teens. Midcon pipes were steady to down slightly in the high-$1.90s. New York city gate weekend gas was flat in the $2.35-2.40 range.
NYMEX said 12,564 contracts traded as of 1145 EDT.
On KCBT, July jumped eight cents to $2.03, while deferreds stayed steady to 3.5 cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by one cent to 12.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
